([[Charlotte, North Carolina]]) | college = *[[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] (2011–2012) *[[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2013–2016) | draft_year = 2016 | career_start = 2016 | years1 = 2016–2017 | team1 = [[Yeşilgiresun Belediye|Yeşilgiresun]] | years2 = 2017–2020 | team2 = [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] | years3 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team3 = [[Washington Wizards]] | highlights = * [[Associated Press|AP]] Honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2015]]) * 2× Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2015, 2016) }} '''Anthony Remeral Gill''' (born October 17, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Gill played college basketball for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]] and the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==College career== ===Recruiting=== {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2011}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Anthony Gill | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Charlotte, NC]] | highschool = [[Charlotte Christian School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 212 | 40 = | commitdate = 2009-10-27 | rivals stars = 3 | scout stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2011 | rivals ref title = South Carolina 2011 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2011 South Carolina Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | 247 ref title = South Carolina 2011 Basketball Commits | rivals school = southcarolina | scout s = 184 | espn schoolid = 2579 | 247 school = | scout overall = 91 | rivals overall = 144 | espn overall = 88 | 247 overall = 95 | accessdate = October 18, 2015 | bball = yes }} ===South Carolina=== [[File:George Washington vs UVA DSC 5992 (15233403623).jpg|thumb|upright=.65|Gill blocking a shot in November 2014]] Gill played in all 31 of South Carolina's games and started in 26 of them. Following the firing of head coach [[Darrin Horn]], Gill was given permission to transfer from South Carolina.{{cite web|title=Gill Granted Permission to Discuss Potential Transfer|url=http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040612aaa.html|website=gamecocksonline.com|publisher=South Carolina Gamecocks|accessdate=October 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180410134914/http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040612aaa.html|archive-date=April 10, 2018|url-status=dead}} ===Virginia=== Gill received interest from [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] and [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|North Carolina]] but ultimately elected to transfer to the [[University of Virginia]].{{cite web |last=Ferber |first=Justin |date=April 23, 2012 |title=Virginia lands Anthony Gill |url=http://www.streakingthelawn.com/2012/4/23/2969186/virginia-lands-anthony-gill |accessdate=October 18, 2015 |website=streakingthelawn.com}} After sitting out his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] season, Gill played an important role off the bench for the Cavaliers during a season where the team won both the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] regular season and [[2014 ACC men's basketball tournament|tournament]] titles. He injured his ankle during Virginia's loss to [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the Sweet Sixteen round of the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|last=White|first=Jeff|title=Curtain Falls on an Extraordinary Basketball Season|url=http://news.virginia.edu/content/curtain-falls-extraordinary-basketball-season|website=UVA Today|publisher=University of Virginia|accessdate=October 18, 2015|date=March 29, 2014}} During his junior season, Gill led the Cavaliers in rebounding with 6.5 rebounds per game and ranked third in scoring with 11.6 points per game. Following the season, he was named third-team All-ACC and voted onto the coaches' All-ACC Defensive Team.{{cite web|title=ACSMA 2015 ALL-ACC BASKETBALL TEAMS ANNOUNCED|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|website=The ACC|accessdate=October 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425010314/http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|archive-date=April 25, 2015|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Yeşilgiresun Belediye (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Gill signed with [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] in Germany. However, he left the team prior to the season's start after failing a medical exam on August 23, 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/anthony-gill-abgereist/|title=Anthony Gill abgereist|work=mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de|date=August 23, 2016|accessdate=August 24, 2016|language=German|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924010913/http://www.mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/anthony-gill-abgereist/|archive-date=September 24, 2016|url-status=dead}} Gill then signed with [[Yeşilgiresun Belediye]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].{{cite web |title=Home |url=http://www.beobasket.net/news/35788/anthony-gill-signed-contract-with-yesilgiresun-from-turkey.html |access-date=June 29, 2017 |archive-date=December 11, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161211065340/http://beobasket.net/news/35788/anthony-gill-signed-contract-with-yesilgiresun-from-turkey.html |url-status=dead }} ===Khimki (2017–2020)=== On June 24, 2017, Gill signed a contract to play for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] during the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |date=June 24, 2017 |title=Anthony Gill Signs with Hornets for NBA Summer League |url=http://www.nbc29.com/story/35742442/anthony-gill-signs-with-hornets-for-nba-summer-league |accessdate=June 29, 2017 |website=nbc29.com |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625032819/http://www.nbc29.com/story/35742442/anthony-gill-signs-with-hornets-for-nba-summer-league |url-status=dead }} He later signed with [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] of the [[VTB United League]]. On August 3, 2020, Gill parted ways with the team.{{cite news |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano |date=August 3, 2020 |title=Anthony Gill officially leaves Khimki |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/anthony-gill-officially-leaves-khimki/ |accessdate=August 3, 2020 |website=Sportando}} ===Washington Wizards (2020–2026)=== On December 1, 2020, Gill signed a two-year contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Rosen|title=Wizards sign Anthony Gill|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-anthony-gill|website=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2020}} He made 26 appearances (four starts) for Washington during the [[2020–21 NBA season]], averaging 3.1 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 0.4 assists. Gill played in 44 contests for the Wizards during the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 4.1 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. On July 1, 2022, Gill signed another two-year contract with the Wizards.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Wizards Sign Anthony Gill To Two-Year Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/wizards-to-sign-anthony-gill-to-two-year-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=January 28, 2024}} He made 59 appearances (eight starts) for the team during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], averaging 3.3 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. Gill made 50 appearances for Washington, including three starts, during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 3.8 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 0.7 assists. On July 25, 2024, Gill re-signed with Washington.{{cite web|title=Wizards Re-sign Anthony Gill|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-re-sign-anthony-gill-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2024|access-date=July 25, 2024}} He played in 51 games for the Wizards during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 2.5 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. Gill was waived by Washington on June 29, 2025.{{cite web |author1=RotoWire Staff |title=Anthony Gill: Getting let go by Washington |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/anthony-gill-getting-let-go-by-washington/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=July 6, 2025 |date=June 30, 2025}} On August 7, 2025, Gill re-signed with the Wizards on a one-year contract.{{Cite web|title=Wizards Re-Sign Anthony Gill|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-re-sign-anthony-gill-3|access-date=October 7, life== Gill was born October 17, 1992, to Sandi Summers and Anthony Gill. He has a brother named Daxton and two sisters named Nichole and Kaytlyn. Gill was born with nerve damage, resulting in the temporary paralysis of the right side of his face.{{cite web|last=Reid|first=Whitey|title=Virginia's Gill smiles through life's adversities|url=http://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-s-gill-smiles-through-life-s-adversities/article_39955198-8929-11e3-a4ce-001a4bcf6878.html|website=dailyprogress.com|date=January 30, 2014 |publisher=The Daily Progress|accessdate=October 18, 2015}} Although rarely a starter in the NBA, Gill is known as a consummate teammate and positive influence on the team, particularly the younger players. "You could write a book on how great of a teammate Anthony Gill is", Wizards coach [[Brian Keefe]] said in January, 2025.{{cite web | last=Shankar | first=Varun | title=How one of the NBA's best teammates has lifted the Wizards | website=The Washington Post | date=2025-04-08 | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2025/04/08/anthony-gill-wizards-best-teammate/ | access-date=2025-12-03}} Off the court, Gill has a reputation of being a prankster. He often makes up stories during interviews, such as owning a two-headed Siamese cat and being a magician in his free time.{{cite web |last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |date=August 18, 2015 |title=The Returnees: Welcome back, Anthony Gill |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/108395 |accessdate=January 28, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/anthony_gill_809110.html Virginia Cavaliers bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013144415/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/anthony_gill_809110.html |date=October 13, 2016 }} * [https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=008001 EuroLeague profile] * {{instagram|anthonygill.13}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Gill, Anthony}} [[Category:1992 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Russia]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Turkey]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Charlotte, North Carolina]] [[Category:BC Khimki players]] [[Category:Charlotte Christian School alumni]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from High Point, North Carolina]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Washington Wizards players]] [[Category:Yeşilgiresun Belediye players]]
